title: I looped a clip with -stream_loop. Is it seamless?
fullTitle: FFmpeg -stream_loop: the Loop Length Follows the Audio

scenes.narration: You loop a four second clip with dash stream loop two. Three plays, so twelve seconds, and no seam. Is the loop seamless? Is the length what you expect? We mark every frame and every audio sample, and read what comes out.

The picture is one hundred twenty marked frames. The audio is a ramp where every sample says where it came from. Control: with both four seconds long, the loop is exactly three hundred sixty frames, twelve seconds, and matches a concat demuxer build. Readers: f f probe packets, and a decode.
captions: Same as the concat demuxer control.

scenes.narration: Now the audio is three point nine seconds, a hundred milliseconds short. Re-encoded, the three plays last eleven point eight three seconds, not twelve. Only three hundred fifty five of three hundred sixty frames survive: the second play starts at frame two, the third at frame three. The loop follows the audio.

With the audio four point one seconds, the loop is twelve point three seconds, and the picture freezes about a hundred thirty milliseconds at each seam. With dash c copy and the short audio, the picture is twelve seconds, but the sound has a hundred millisecond hole at each seam.
captions: Audio 4.1 s: 12.3 s, picture holes 0.13 s.
-c copy, audio 3.9 s: 0.1 s sound holes.

scenes.narration: With an infinite loop and dash t twenty five, the length is exact: twenty five seconds, seven hundred fifty frames. With the short audio it is exact too, but every play after the first loses its first two or three frames. Sound and picture stay within thirty three milliseconds. No drift.

Before you loop, compare the audio length and the picture length. When they match, the loop is exact. Not tested: other ffmpeg builds, other containers and codecs, real footage with encoder delay, stream order, and any player.
captions: Match audio and picture lengths first.
Not tested: other builds, real footage.
